findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of 12 randomized trials (835 patients) reported greater global symptom improvement with peppermint oil versus placebo (risk ratio 2.39, 95% CI 1.93 to 2.97), with a number needed to treat of three.
findings.limitations: 835 patients across 12 trials; enteric-coated formulations dominate the evidence

findings.finding_summary: The same meta-analysis reported improved abdominal pain versus placebo (risk ratio 1.78, 95% CI 1.43 to 2.20), number needed to treat of four.
Across eight randomized trials in the same meta-analysis, reported adverse effects did not differ significantly between peppermint oil and placebo.

This meta-analysis of five randomized controlled trials reported that Saccharomyces boulardii reduced the risk of antibiotic-associated diarrhoea from 17.2% to 6.7%, roughly one case prevented per ten treated.
findings.limitations: five trials; effect sizes vary by population and antibiotic

findings.endpoint: antibiotic-associated diarrhea in hospitalized elderly patients
findings.finding_summary: In this single-center randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial, Saccharomyces boulardii was reported as not effective in preventing antibiotic-associated diarrhea in hospitalized elderly patients.
findings.limitations: population-attribution of the null to this specific trial should be confirmed during verification

findings.finding_summary: This review reported meta-analytic evidence that Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG reduced antibiotic-associated diarrhea risk from 22.4% to 12.3% versus placebo or no treatment.
findings.limitations: when children and adults were analyzed separately, the difference was significant only in children

findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 randomized trials (1,278 pregnant women) reported significantly improved nausea symptoms with ginger versus placebo, with no significant increase in spontaneous-abortion risk.
findings.limitations: subgroup analyses favored daily doses below 1,500 mg for nausea relief

findings.finding_summary: The same meta-analysis reported that ginger did not significantly reduce the number of vomiting episodes versus placebo, with a non-significant trend toward improvement.

This systematic review of 23 randomized trials reported no overall significant differences in acute or delayed nausea and vomiting with ginger, while the subgroup taking up to 1 g/day for more than four days had significantly less acute vomiting.
findings.limitations: the positive result is a dose-and-duration subgroup, not the overall comparison

findings.endpoint: symptom response in postinfectious IBS-D with intestinal hyperpermeability
findings.population: adults with postinfectious diarrhea-predominant IBS and increased intestinal permeability
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial, the primary symptom-response endpoint was reached by 79.6% on glutamine versus 5.8% on placebo in this narrowly defined post-infectious population.
findings.limitations: highly selected population (post-enteric-infection IBS-D with documented hyperpermeability); the unusually large effect awaits independent replication

findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis reported that glutamine supplementation did not significantly affect intestinal permeability overall.
findings.limitations: contrasts with positive results in selected subpopulations such as the postinfectious IBS-D trial

findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials reported significant improvements with inulin in stool frequency, stool consistency, and transit time in chronic constipation.
findings.limitations: pooled standardized effects with wide confidence intervals (stool frequency effect 0.69, 95% CI 0.04 to 1.34)

findings.endpoint: bowel habit in functional constipation (12 g/day)
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study, 12 g daily inulin improved stool frequency and abdominal well-being and shifted gut microbiota toward butyrate-producing genera.
findings.limitations: pain and bloating were reported as not improving with inulin intake

findings.endpoint: daily crying time in infantile colic (weeks 2-3)
findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of six randomized trials (423 infants) reported reduced crying time with L. reuteri DSM 17938 at two weeks (about 43 fewer minutes/day) and three weeks (about 46 fewer minutes/day), with no serious adverse events.
findings.limitations: trial heterogeneity noted by the authors; effect not maintained at four weeks

findings.endpoint: colic treatment effectiveness at four weeks
findings.finding_summary: The same meta-analysis reported that the increased treatment effectiveness seen at two and three weeks was no longer significant at four weeks, consistent with gradual physiological improvement of colic.
